rationale: C3 is G.O.(Ms) No.50 dated 23.05.2016 ordering the waiver of outstanding crop, medium-term and long-term loans of small and marginal farmers with cooperative banks. C1 and C2 issue the guidelines (28.6.2016). C4 reports 12,02,075 farmers benefited (Rs.5318.73 crore). Scope matches the promise.

C2 reports cooperative crop loans of Rs.4,227.98 crore disbursed during 2016-17, against a Rs.6,000 crore target (C1). Only one year is shown, below the pace needed for Rs.40,000 crore over five years; cumulative achievement is not shown.

C4 and C2 report that during 2016-17 and 2017-18 the State bears the interest subsidy and farmers repaying on time pay no interest on crop loans. This matches the promise to continue full subsidy. No GO is shown, so the date is the policy note date of C4.

I1 fulfilled 2016-07-04; I2 fulfilled 2016. C4 is a GO of 2016-07-04 sanctioning the Blue Green Algae production and distribution scheme for 2016-17, an early dated official step. C3 reports the Government has launched a Food Grain Mission and other production schemes, without dates. C2 is only budget intent. Evidence of launches is thin and mostly undated.

C2 reports subsidised distribution of certified seeds to farmers (scheme implemented 2017-18); C4 is a GO (2018-08-31) fixing per-kg distribution subsidy on certified oilseeds. C1, C3 and C5 show continued procurement and subsidy. Scope matches the promise.

I1 not_started; I2 not_started. C1 to C3 (policy notes) describe women producer groups under TNSRLM and proposals to form more, with no order. C4 permits custom hiring centres by women producer groups, and C5 concerns farmer producer groups of small and marginal farmers, not an order expanding farm women groups. Related activity only.

C3 (GO Ms No.65, 2018-03-10) sanctions Rs.800 lakh for SMAM machinery in 2017-18, the earliest sanction after office in these extracts. C1, C4 and C5 show continued annual sanctions in 2020-21. The scheme was continued.

I1 not_started; I2 not_started. C1 is a budget speech saying a special pulse programme will be launched, which is only an announcement. C5 is a GO for the national food security mission pulses component, a broader existing programme rather than the special self-sufficiency mission. No order launching the special mission shown.

I1 fulfilled 2017-02-07; I2 fulfilled 2018-07-12. C2 is a 2016 budget announcement of a special self-sufficiency pulse programme (intent only). C4 is the GO of 07.02.2017 sanctioning a special package for pulses cultivation with Rs.50 crore dovetailed funds over 60,000 acres, the first dated official step. It is a package rather than a named mission, so some doubt remains.

C5 is a 2017-03-10 GO sanctioning financial assistance for procuring agricultural machinery under SMAM for 2016-17, after the government took office. C1 reports subsidy continuing in 2017-18 and proposed for 2018-19; C2 and C3 show it continuing to 2020-21. Continuation of the subsidy is shown.

C5 (G.O.Ms.No.290, 2016-09-23) releases the first instalment for the 2016-17 micro irrigation scheme; C4 (2017-02-07) states 100% subsidy for small and marginal farmers and 75% for others; C1 and C2 confirm the State continued these rates.

I1 fulfilled 2017-09-21; I2 fulfilled 2018-01-23. C1 states the Rainfed Area Development scheme aims to enhance the income of rainfed farmers. C3 shows the first instalment was sanctioned by the Government Order read third, G.O.(Ms).No.238 dated 21.09.2017, with later GOs (C2, C3, C4) continuing it. A dedicated order exists; whether the scheme is new is uncertain.

The promise does not say which scheme is to be expanded, so no extract can be tied to it. The extracts cover coffee growers, house building advance, dryland clusters, house repair and horticulture schemes, none identified as the one meant.

C1 reports a NABARD-sanctioned project (from 2017-18) building water harvesting structures in Chittar sub-basin, and reclamation of saline problem soils (Cuddalore, Ramanathapuram, Tirunelveli). These cover parts of water systems and land reclamation, but only in a few districts, and no GO date is given. C2 is a 2012 wasteland scheme with no allotment. Partial; date is year-level only.

C2 reports the Sustainable Sugarcane Initiative scheme was promoted during 2017-18 (shade nets installed, seedlings distributed) and is programmed for 2018-19. C1 and C3 show related continuing support. The scheme predates this government, so the date only marks evidence of continued implementation within 2017-18.

C1, C2 and C3 discuss horticulture schemes and input supply in general, and C3 lists an input supply system as a strategy. None shows a GO or dedicated step on timely quality inputs for horticulture and hill crops; C4 and C5 concern extension and review committees.

The promise does not name the fund. C1 describes the ESI revolving fund created in 2004 and its use in 2016-17, with no order raising it or widening its service. C2, C4 (UIDSSMT revolving fund) and C3, C5 (startup revolving grant) concern other funds and beneficiaries.

C5 (G.O. 95, 13.05.2020) orders a Rs.2500 lakh incentive scheme for sensitive horticulture crops with price forecasting, aimed at assured returns. It covers selected crops only and does not show farmers receiving good prices. C1-C4 are general marketing or non-horticultural price support.

The promise only says to expand an unnamed scheme, so no extract can be matched to it as the same action for the same object. The extracts concern horticulture, supply chain, house building advance and similar unrelated schemes.

C1 and C3 are about specialised market complexes for tender coconut, banana, mango, grapes and vegetables, but they are policy-note descriptions with no dated GO, sanction or launch showing when each was set up, so a step after 2016-05-23 cannot be shown. Complexes may predate this government.

C1 (GO of 2017-08-31) recalls the 2016-17 sanction of pumps up to 10 HP at 80% subsidy and sanctions 1000 more at 90% for 5-10 HP. C3 sanctions 500 more at 90% in 2018-19. The subsidy was continued at or above 80%. The 2016-17 sanction itself has no exact date.

C5 is GO Ms.No.32 of 2018-02-08 sanctioning 46 godowns in Regulated Markets for farmers. C3 reports cold storage facilities created. Both warehouses and cold storage are covered, though the earliest dated order shown is for godowns.

The promise names no object (Build these in greater numbers), so it cannot be matched to any extract. The extracts cover an industrial policy, cold storage, check dams and a house building advance, none identifiably what was promised.

C5 sanctions pulses processing units in cooperative marketing societies and C2 mentions pulses drying units, but neither procures or sells farmers' pulses. C1 and C4 cover copra procurement, a different crop. No step for procuring and selling pulses through cooperatives is shown.

I1 diluted 2020-07-22; I2 diluted 2020-07-22. C4 is a GO (2020-07-22) sanctioning the Cotton Cultivation Mission to increase cotton production, but its target is raising area to 6 lakh acres from about 4 lakh and ELS area to 30,000 Ha, far below a twofold production increase (C5, C1). The mission pre-dates the government (2014-15). So an order exists, with materially reduced scope.

I1 fulfilled 2016-12-30; I2 fulfilled 2018-12-31. Directional promise. C5 is a GO dated 2016-12-30 giving administrative approval to a coconut garden replanting and rejuvenation scheme costing Rs.20 crore, a dedicated measure for coconut growers. C2 is a later GO (2018-12-31) sanctioning a livelihood package for coconut farmers.

I1 fulfilled 2017-06-29; I2 fulfilled 2017-06-29. C2 is the GO of 2017-06-29 laying down the procedure for forming Farmers Interest Groups and 2,000 Farmer Producer Groups (guidelines for forming many associations). C4 confirms the scheme continuing with 2,000 new FPGs. Matches the indicator.

C5 shows the first-read GO dated 06.07.2016 giving administrative approval for Coconut Development Board schemes in 2016-17, including the integrated farming for productivity scheme. C2 reports 3.25 lakh hybrid coconut seedlings produced and distributed, and C1 and C5 give further sanctions. Both elements of the promise are covered.

C3 and C1 mention Coconut Producers Societies/Company only in the context of Neera licensing and planned training. C4 and C5 are GOs on general farmer producer groups and organisations, not coconut producer companies. No order establishing coconut producer companies or coconut production training is shown.

The coconut GOs (C1 to C5) approve Coconut Development Board assisted schemes at a total outlay of Rs.187.50 lakh, with nurseries and demonstration plots. That is a far smaller, different scheme from a Rs.800 crore special scheme to cut and replant old coconut trees. No such step shown.

C5 is a GO (30.12.2016) for cutting and removal of old, senile, diseased palms and replanting, but at Rs.20 crore on pilot basis versus the promised Rs.800 crore. C2/C4 Gaja package targets cyclone damage, not the promised scheme. Materially reduced scope.

I1 fulfilled 2017-02-07; I2 fulfilled 2018-01-22. C1 is a GO dated 2017-02-07 sanctioning funds to train registered organic farmers and operators on organic standards. It is a dedicated organic-farming measure, though small in scale.

No extract mentions genetically modified crops or any ban or non-permission of them. C1 is bio-control agents, C2 borewells for horticulture, C3 and C4 crop insurance, C5 Kuruvai package. None is about the commitment.
No extract is about barring genetically modified crops. C1 only lists GM seeds as a law syllabus topic; C2, C3 and C5 are seed, cashew and oilseed scheme sanctions; C4 is crop insurance.

C3 reports a scheme introduced with effect from 24.06.2017 for free agricultural service connections, plus 30,835 connections in 2017-18; C1 and C5 show free power to farmers continuing. Continuation of free farm electricity is implemented.

No extract concerns methane or shale gas projects or any state decision barring schemes that affect delta farmers. C1, C3 and C4 describe bio-gas plant subsidies and rural programmes; C2 is a cyclone fuel advance; C5 is a solar pump scheme. None is about this commitment.

No extract is about gas pipelines or restricting them from agricultural lands. C1 and C3 describe permission to lay pipelines and optical fibre cables in Government lands (with track rent exempt for agricultural water pipes), which is a different subject. Other extracts concern land ceiling, rice fallow and dryland schemes.

C1 is the GO dated 2016-07-21 giving administrative sanction to PMFBY, replacing NAIS, with higher state premium subsidy. C3 confirms implementation from Kharif 2016 with wider risk cover. Scheme is a central one adopted by the state, so 'enhanced' is met by wider cover.

C5 is the GO of 2019-10-21 sanctioning marketing infrastructure in 90 regulated markets and records e-trading in 30 of 282 regulated markets. C1 shows only pilot e-trading in 2017. Some regulated markets are covered, not all, so partial.

C1 (2019 policy note) lists SMS dissemination of market prices as an ongoing departmental activity; C3 describes the same activity before. No GO, launch or new scheme is shown, so this is the same activity carrying on with no official step.

I1 fulfilled 2016-06-21; I2 fulfilled 2017-06-29. C1 reports administrative sanction issued on 21.06.2016 for the supply chain management project, which creates post-harvest infrastructure and backward and forward linkages for fruits and vegetables. C3 (Food Processing Policy GO, 2018) confirms the network of primary processing centres being established. The order was issued after the government took office.

C4 is G.O.Ms.No.169 of 2016-06-21 sanctioning Rs.398.75 crore for supply chain infrastructure for fruits and vegetables in 10 districts; C3 describes the primary processing centres with cold storage, and C1 reports cold storage facilities created across the State. Scope is broadly as promised, though the main project covers 10 districts.

No extract concerns an increased procurement price for paddy. C1-C3 are copra procurement under a price support scheme, and C4, C5 are NFSM paddy input and seed subsidies, which are not procurement prices. Nothing is about the commitment.

C1-C3 policy notes report a state incentive over MSP and that sums 'have been provided as incentive'; no GO or official order raising the paddy procurement price is in the extracts. C4/C5 concern copra and green gram.

C2 (GO of 2017-01-05) fixes the 2016-17 State Advised Price at Rs.2,850, the same figure as the 2015-16 price it recalls, so no increase is shown. C1 and C3 move to revenue sharing with a transitional incentive that holds the earlier price. Only related steps, none a higher SAP.

C3 reports the 2018 Act enacted so farmers get Fair and Remunerative Price in time, and incentives disbursed to farmers. C2 (GO of 2020-04-03) sanctions Rs.106 crore to mills on condition it clears farmers' FRP arrears. State action was taken, though arrears persisted. The Act is dated by year only.
C3 is GO (Ms) No.56 of 2016-06-10 ordering copra procurement at MSP because the open-market price was lower. C1 shows the scheme being implemented again in 2021 for a price fall. Matches the promise.

C3 and C5 show the state pressing the Union and the Supreme Court for the Cauvery Management Board and Regulation Committee, which only the Union can constitute, and C3 says they were not yet constituted. C2 and C5 show the Court directing the Union to frame a scheme. No extract shows full implementation.

The state pressed the issue in the Supreme Court and obtained an order (C1, 20.9.2016), but the Court deferred the constitution of the Board on 4.10.2016 (C1). C5 shows the 16.02.2018 judgement directed the Union to frame a scheme. Constitution of the Board and Committee rests with the Union, and the extracts do not show it.

The state acted: administrative sanction of Rs.7.85 crore for strengthening Baby Dam (C4, C5), works split and tenders finalised. Clearances from Union ministries are pending (C4, C5) and the Supreme Court allows 152 ft only after strengthening and expert examination (C2, C3). The level reached only 142 ft (C1).

C5: the state objected to the Mekedatu dam, filed a Supreme Court application (30.11.2018) and a contempt petition, and the CM wrote to the PM (24.06.2019). Despite this, the Central Water Commission allowed Karnataka to prepare the DPR, and the cases are pending. The state acted, but prevention depended on the Union and the courts. C1-C4 report steps from before the government took office.

C2 shows the state formally objected to Kerala's Pattisserry dam work through the Chief Minister's letters to the Prime Minister and a Supreme Court application. C5 shows a Supreme Court decree restraining Kerala at Mullai Periyar. Outcome rests with the Union and courts and is not shown settled.

I1 fulfilled 2016-09-23; I2 not_started. C5: on 23.9.2016 Tamil Nadu filed objections in the Supreme Court Cauvery case over Karnataka's water releases. C3: on 31.03.2018 it filed a contempt petition to enforce the Cauvery water scheme. C4: on 20.11.2017 it filed a civil appeal against Kerala's works in the Mullai Periyar area. The earliest in-term filing is C5.

C1 and C4 show the state repeatedly pressing the Union government, while the Union took no steps to implement river linking. The state acted but delivery rests with the Union. Extracts address only the national interlinking project.

C3 lists a Special Committee meeting on 26.07.2016, after the government took office, where the state pressed for immediate river linking. C2 shows later letters by the Chief Minister to the Union Minister and Prime Minister. Formal urging done.

Only C4 touches river linking: a budget speech line urging the Union on national river linkage projects generally, without naming the Pamba-Achankovil-Vaippar link and not as a formal step such as a resolution or letter. C1-C3, C5 are unrelated.

C3 records that the Chief Minister's memorandum to the Prime Minister of 14.06.2016, after the government took office, urged the Government of India to implement the Pamba-Achankoil-Vaippar link. C2 and C1 add the 27.2.2017 memorandum and 24.05.2017 letter. A formal advocacy step was taken.

C4 is the GO of 05.01.2018 permitting construction of 20,000 check dams. C2 and C3 show dam and canal rehabilitation works in progress. Barrage construction appears only as a detailed project report under consideration (C1), so that component is not shown as implemented. Dates for dam rehabilitation start are not given.

I1 fulfilled 2019-06-13; I2 fulfilled 2018-01-05. The GO in C3 (2019-06-13) sanctions Rs.499.688 crore for Kudimaramath works, including strengthening tank bunds and desilting. C4 reports 1,200 tanks taken up for desilting and bund restoration in 2016-17, but it is an undated policy note, so the date comes from C3, the earliest dated sanction.

I1 not_started; I2 not_started; I3 not_started. C1 is a budget speech saying flood prevention works will be taken up in Cuddalore. That is an announcement, not an order. C2 is a Governor's address, C4 is a command area programme order unrelated to flood storage or salt water intrusion. No order to complete these works shown.

I1 not_started; I2 not_started; I3 partial 2016-12-13. C2 lists preventing sea water intrusion as a goal of a disaster management perspective plan, which is a statement of intent, not an order to complete works. No extract shows a GO or sanction to complete flood storage or salt water intrusion works.

I1 unverifiable; I2 unverifiable. The promise and indicator do not name the project, and the extracts concern unrelated subjects (Mekedatu litigation, Chennai Metro cost, ROB works, a Tambaram bypass). No extract can be tied to the commitment.

The promise text 'Fulfill these works' names no work, object or beneficiary. The extracts cover MGNREGS works, the Self Sufficiency Scheme, child labour and irrigation works, none of which can be tied to the commitment, so no extract is about it.

The promise says 'this reservoir' without naming it, so no extract can be tied to it. C1 mentions a reservoir scheme nearing completion, but nothing links it to this commitment; the other extracts cover desilting, check dams and building rules.

C1 (2017-07-09) reports PMKSY repair and restoration of tanks in Vellore, Ramanathapuram and Sivagangai taken up at Rs.27.30 crore; C2 reports 104 tanks in those three districts completed. C4 and C5 add Kudimaramath restoration GOs for them in 2019. Treating tanks as the lakes of the promise; the date is the earliest document reporting the works under way.

C2 reports administrative sanction for the Athikadavu Avinashi scheme at Rs.1652.00 crore on a DBOT basis, with the intake structure and pipeline only proposed. C1 and C3 show earlier sanctions for investigation and clearances in progress. No sign of works or operation yet.

I1 partial 2018-01-05; I2 fulfilled 2018-01-05. C4 is GO (Ms) No.6 of 2018-01-05 permitting 20,000 check dams and approving guidelines. Desilting is only mentioned in an undated policy note (C2), with no dated order, so only the check-dam part is clearly ordered.

I1 unverifiable; I2 unverifiable. The promise only says 'this project' with no identifiable subject. The extracts concern unrelated projects (an industrial corridor unit, rural sanitation, a bus project, metro rail, a health reform programme), so none can be tied to the commitment.

C1, C2 and C3 report sub-centres created and dispensaries opened or upgraded, but only as cumulative figures since 2011-12 with no dated order or launch inside this term. C4 and C5 are unrelated GOs. No dated official step by this government is shown.

C1 is an undated policy note saying efforts are being taken to organise new societies, and C4 only says societies will be formed after cow distribution. Neither shows a GO or registration of new societies. C5 funds buildings for existing societies.

C1 reports cold rooms, milk coolers and a Madurai dairy expansion under way; C3 reports 341 coolers installed and 218 more proposed; C4 only proposes a new Madhavaram dairy. No dated GO or sanction for a large new dairy or chillers appears, so only works in progress are shown.

C1 is the 2016-09-16 GO sanctioning the 2016-17 free goat/sheep scheme, 4 animals per beneficiary. C2 is the 2020-21 sanction (head of account for persons below the poverty line), and C5 the 2019-20 sanction, showing yearly continuation.

C1 (and C5) is the GO dated 26.08.2019 sanctioning free distribution of 12,000 milch cows for 2019-20, an official continuation of the scheme; C2-C4 policy notes report the scheme continuing. The earliest GO in the extracts is C1.

C1 is the GO of 2019-09-05 sanctioning Rs.25 crore for the State Fodder Development Scheme in 2019-20; C4 reports the scheme continuing. The earlier policy notes (C3, C5) describe continuation but are not GOs, so the first GO shown is C1.

C1 to C3 show the 25% subsidy scheme launched in 2012-13, before this government, continuing with money sanctioned in a policy note. No GO or new scheme launch in the term is shown for broiler and native chicken farms. C4 and C5 cover backyard Aseel birds, a different scheme.

C5 is a GO dated 2020-02-25 sanctioning inland fish landing centres. C1 reports completed dredging at fishing harbour basins and landing centre basins at Rs.17.80 crore, and a sanctioned feasibility study for new harbours. Both parts are addressed, but the only dated order is C5.

The promise refers only to 'these schemes' without naming any scheme, and none of C1-C5 can be matched to a specific commitment. Extracts cover general Governor's address policy, Self Sufficiency Scheme guidelines, NFSM guidelines and MSME growth parks; nothing is about this commitment.
The commitment ('Continuously implement these schemes') does not say which schemes. None of C1-C5 can be tied to it.

I1 in_progress; I2 in_progress. Directional. C1 says an inland fisheries policy has been framed and is under the Government's consideration, which is a preparatory step. C4 is a GO on inland fish landing centres (landing infrastructure, not production). C2 and C3 are policy-note descriptions of continuing activity. No order giving priority to inland fish production is shown.

C5 is a GO (16.07.2018) giving administrative and financial sanction for the Fisheries University's project proposals (technology park, referral laboratory). C2 lists projects carried out in 2018-19, including a Fisheries Training Institute and para-professional institute. C1 covers works from 2015-16, before the government took office. 'Improve' has no defined target, so these steps count as fulfilment.

C2 (2016-09-29) shows 2016-17 fishing ban relief sanctioned and already disbursed to over 1.5 lakh families, with schemes continued; C5 (GO 56, 2019-05-27) and C4 (GO 142, 2019-10-22) sanction later relief, and C3 reports enhanced relief. The relief schemes continued and grew. Only the year 2016 is supported.

C3 (budget speech) promises enhancement of both schemes to Rs.5,000. C2 (policy note) says the CM ordered it and both amounts have been enhanced to Rs.5,000 but will be implemented this year. It reports a decision, with no GO or disbursement at the new rate shown.

C3 (budget speech) promises enhancement of both schemes to Rs.5,000. C2 (policy note) says the CM ordered it and both amounts have been enhanced to Rs.5,000 but will be implemented this year. It reports a decision, with no GO or disbursement at the new rate shown.

C5 says Rs.5000 is paid for fishing ban relief from 2017 onwards; C2 says orders raised it from Rs.2,000 and the lean season allowance from Rs.4,000 to Rs.5,000. C1 shows both at Rs.5,000. Exact GO date not given, so year only.

C1 is G.O.(Ms) No.40 of 2017-02-20 approving a separate fishermen housing scheme of 5000 houses at Rs.85 crore, citing the 2016 manifesto. C4 reports 3098 fisherfolk benefitted and the scheme extended, so it is operating.

No extract concerns including the fishermen community in the Scheduled Tribes list or any urging of the Union on it. C1 is about Palk Bay and Jallikattu, C2 and C3 about existing Scheduled Tribes, C4 and C5 about a fishermen relief scheme.

I1 not_started; I2 not_started. Extracts are welfare relief orders (fishing ban and lean season relief, savings-cum-relief) and general policy note aims on sea safety. None is a dedicated order on protecting fishermen.
The commitment ('Implement this scheme') does not name the scheme. None of C1-C5 can be identified as being about it.

C5 is GO 115 dated 2017-05-23 giving administrative approval and financial sanction of Rs.286 crore for subsidised deep sea fishing boats. C2 gives the 70% subsidy per boat. This is a subsidy to buy mechanised fishing boats.
The promise ('these schemes') has no identifiable object. C1/C5 (house repair), C2/C4 (fisheries welfare) and C3 (MLACDS) cannot be tied to a specific commitment.

I1 in_progress; I2 in_progress. C1 and C2 report land allotment orders for fish processing parks and orders for retender, with works in progress in one district. The orders are undated in the extracts and the parks are not yet operational, so only an in-progress step can be credited and no realisation date can be given.

Directional advocacy commitment. C1 records the Chief Minister's memorandum to the Prime Minister on 14.6.2016, after the government took office, on Katchatheevu and traditional fishing rights; C2 says memoranda reiterated the need for retrieval and gives the Assembly resolutions. A formal state step on the same issue was taken.

Directional advocacy commitment. C1 records the Chief Minister's memorandum to the Prime Minister on 14.6.2016, after the government took office, on Katchatheevu and traditional fishing rights; C2 says memoranda reiterated the need for retrieval and gives the Assembly resolutions. A formal state step on the same issue was taken.

C2 records the Chief Minister's memorandum to the Prime Minister on 14.6.2016, after taking office, on Katchatheevu and fishing rights, and reiterates the retrieval stand. For a directional advocacy promise this formal step counts. The resolutions of 2013 and 2014 predate office.

C2 reports that the Tamil Nadu Government facilitated the fourth round of talks between Tamil Nadu and Sri Lankan fishermen on 02.11.2016, after taking office, on the arrest issue. It is a dedicated official measure for a directional promise, though the problem itself persists.

C2 (G.O.(Ms) No.146, 2020-06-02) accords administrative sanction of Rs.52.46 crore for 7 groynes at Alanthalai, a village subject to sea erosion. C5 reports groyne works built or in progress in Thoothukudi, Kanniyakumari and Thiruvallur districts. This is action to construct groynes at erosion-prone places; earlier GOs are not dated in the extracts.

Directional commitment. Only C1 (Governor's address) mentions Jallikattu, as a statement of intent that earnest efforts will be made. It is not a GO, bill, resolution or other dedicated measure. C2 to C5 are unrelated.

Directional commitment. C1 reports the state issued an Ordinance amending the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act to enable Jallikattu; C3 confirms the Tamil Nadu amendment Act, 2017 and Jallikattu Rules, 2017, with events conducted. A dedicated law exists; only the year (2017) is shown.

C1 shows the Uzhavar Pathukappu Thittam (started 2011) still being implemented, with registration continuing and members counted as on 29.02.2020, so the scheme was continued. No extract gives an earlier dated step after taking office; date is the dated registration figure in C1. C2-C5 concern other schemes.

I1 not_started; I2 fulfilled 2017; I3 fulfilled 2017. C1 shows the order implementing the coastal disaster risk reduction project was issued on 21.1.2014, before this government took office, so it does not count. No extract shows a new order by this government; C4 and C5 are renaming orders.

No extract is about completing projects estimated at 790 crore rupees by 2018. C5's 790 refers to buildings for access audit, and the others cover unrelated works and schemes, so nothing can be judged.

C3 shows free house-site pattas continuing to be issued each year 2016-17 to 2018-19 and a GO of 27.11.2018 granting 3 cents of free house site to poor families. No earlier dated GO after taking office is shown, so the date is from that GO. C1, C4, C5 concern house construction.

I1 fulfilled 2019-11-12; I2 fulfilled 2019-11-12. C1 (G.O. 428, 12.11.2019) forms the new Kundrathur and Vandalur taluks; C3 (G.O. 424, same date) forms Thiruvennainallur and Kalvarayan Hills taluks. These are orders creating new taluks after the government took office. C4 only reports pre-2016 creations.
No extract concerns the Amma Scheme of government reaching out to people or Amma Service Centres; C1-C5 cover other Amma-branded schemes (skill training, driver training, two-wheelers, canteens).

I1 fulfilled 2018-07-17; I2 fulfilled 2018-07-09. C4 is a Finance Department GO dated 17 July 2018 directing that the existing Scheme of Advances for Education of Government Employees' children be continued for three more years. This matches the indicator (an order to continue an existing scheme). C1 and C3 only state intent to continue. The promise's scheme set is vague.

C3 reports free laptop distribution continuing for 2017-18; C4/C5 show distribution to 11th and 12th std in 2018-19 and 11th std from 2019-20. The scheme was continued for higher secondary students. No GO date given; year from C3.

C1-C3 describe laptop distribution but no internet connection with the laptops. C5 sanctions free internet in 366 government higher secondary schools, which is a related step for schools, not an internet connection given with students' laptops. No official step for the commitment itself.

I1 not_started; I2 not_started. C3 is a Governor's address saying school schemes will continue, which is a statement. C1 and C2 are scheme pages with no order. C4 is a differently abled welfare GO and C5 a pension committee GO, neither for school students. No administrative order continuing school student schemes shown.
I1 not_started; I2 not_started. C1/C4 are policy notes stating schemes will continue; C2, C3, C5 are COVID school-closure GOs. No administrative order continuing student schemes is shown.

I1 fulfilled 2018-05-18; I2 fulfilled 2019-11-07. The GO in C5 (2018-05-18) restructures field administration to ensure effective monitoring of schools and quality of education, a dedicated official measure. The GO in C4 (2019-11-20) sets the Commissioner's functions, including measures to improve quality. C1-C3 are policy-note descriptions.

C1 states the Integrated Learning Scheme through Internet was introduced in high and higher secondary schools in academic year 2016-17, with virtual classrooms provided to 770 government schools and 11 DIETs. Matches the promise. C2-C5 do not concern it.

I1 fulfilled 2017-03-14; I2 in_progress. C3 is G.O.(Ms) No.47 of 2017-03-14 sanctioning Rs.25192.19 lakh for school infrastructure in 149 government high schools; C5 (2019-01-30) is a further financial sanction of Rs.12 crore for infrastructure in tribal schools. Both are funds sanctioned for school infrastructure after the government took office.

C1-C3 show RTE 25% admissions of disadvantaged children in private schools with fee reimbursement continuing after 2016 (admissions in 2017-18, 2018-19, 2019-20; reimbursement to schools). Continuation implemented; year from C2.

I1 fulfilled 2019-10-15; I2 fulfilled 2019-07-26. C1 records that the first GO (No.469 dated 15.10.2019) ordered a new Government Medical College at Tiruppur; C5 reports an order for a new medical college at Namakkal, and C2-C4 cover Krishnagiri, Nilgiris and Dindigul. These are administrative orders establishing new colleges, though only medical colleges are shown.

I1 fulfilled 2021-01-11; I2 fulfilled 2021-01-11. C4 is the GO (Ms) No. 5 of 11.01.2021 adopting UGC regulations on qualifications and measures for maintaining standards in higher education for colleges: a policy guideline on college quality. C1 (03.09.2020) only constitutes a committee to study the National Education Policy, a preparatory step.

I1 not_started; I2 not_started. C3 is a GO for enhancing the State Data Centre cloud and C2 is a cloud web-hosting service for students and entrepreneurs. Neither is an order connecting universities through cloud computing. Related cloud activity only.
